pitch_detail.notes: Enter at ~7,800 ft on the Stuart Glacier and climb as the couloir narrows, with two steeper steps.
Wider snowfield climbing to the West Ridge notch.
Mixed fifth-class rock with ice/snow sections; early season features dry-tooling.
Center of the wall, trending left toward the upper South Rib
20-30 ft sections with decent protection
Hand/finger splitter crack with a chimney, 40m
Hanging corners, arete, crack traverse, 55m
'Monkey Traverse' - exposed horizontal crack, 20m
V-slot with varied stemming, 60m
Corner crack to a belay ledge, 30m
Corner crack, slab, sparse-pro traverse, 55m
'Fifth Avenue' - corner bulge, stem-box, 40m
'Empire State Building' - headwall splitter, 55m
Two 60m pitches of ice below the Hidden Couloir
A few hundred feet trending up and left
Unconsolidated snow over moderate rock; traverse ~30 ft left
Mixed chimney climbing
Steep snow and a final rock band to the summit ridge, joining the North Buttress Couloir line
Entry couloir from ~6,400 ft, hidden from the lake.
Crux: steep ice/mixed pitches connecting 1st to 2nd couloir; can be thin/paper-thin ice over rock.
Broad couloir, exit up and right into the 3rd couloir.
Final couloir pitch to upper mountain.
Short scramble from the top of the 3rd couloir to the summit.
Corner climbing with face moves; 6 bolts.
Face climbing transitioning to a ledge traverse; 13 bolts.
Bolt line trending up and left; 4-5 bolts.
Face climbing with a slight rightward traverse; 7 bolts.
Crux pitch: ledge traverse into a pumpy sequence; 9 bolts; some loose holds reported.
Easier climbing to the rappel-anchor belay; 5 bolts.
Unroped scrambling to the true summit; single bolt en route but no anchor at the top.
Open-book corners beginning north of the Pineapple Pass gully, leading to a left-facing slab.
Locate three cracks leading to a small overhang; face-climb around/left of them.
Easy scrambling to the true summit.
Approach gully to the ridge saddle with scrambling to a chockstone, ~290 ft
Ridge climbing around/over the chockstone on mixed-quality rock, difficult protection, ~350 ft
Continued ridge travel to the summit, ~300 ft
